observations: I read all 13 XML files and the guidelines excerpt. I did not read code, YAML, readings JSON, primary sources or images.

Chapter and verse scope is correct in every file. Verse milestones are consecutive, so adjacent verses share boundaries. Every sequence ends with a verse terminator and then a chapter terminator, before the paragraph or line closes, which follows the rule that a closing tag is not a terminator. In ki_ladonai, each of Psalms 22, Obadiah 1 and Zechariah 14 is terminated separately before the next opens.

Partial chapters use a chapter milestone with n and no corresp, as stated. Under rule 3, a unit-bearing milestone with no corresp counts as a terminator. So the opening chapter milestones end nothing, open nothing and only display a number. Because explicit verse terminators are present, verse scope does not depend on them.

Hebrew and English use the same correspondences in every pair: vayevarekh_david, attah_hu, vayyosha, az_yashir, ki_ladonai and morning_song_shema. These include quoted_exodus_15_11, the quoted/repeated_exodus_15_18 pair and quoted_zechariah_14_9. No canonical Bible verse URN appears twice in a file.

The quotations in az_yashir 15:11 and 15:18 (both prints), ki_ladonai Zechariah 14:9 and morning_song_shema Deuteronomy 6:4 each place the occurrence milestone before a seg that carries the Bible source, as the guidelines require. In the Hebrew az_yashir, each quotation that runs across printed lines is split into one seg per tei:l, each with the same source. This keeps the line structure well-formed, but one quotation becomes several spans.

Hebrew az_yashir keeps the printed poetry layout with lg and l, and the page break to p.30 falls inside a line. English az_yashir is prose (tei:p), and its page break also falls mid-verse. Each attah_hu file has a page break to p.29 inside verse 8. Facsimile page numbers advance consistently (Hebrew n85/87/89, English n86/88/90).

Citation notes are standOff type=citation, and both the target and the ref point at the first verse represented: Chronicles 1 29:10, Nehemiah 9:6, Exodus 14:30 and, in the Hebrew only, Exodus 15:1. English az_yashir has no citation note, as stated. ki_ladonai (both languages), ki_va_sus and morning_song_shema also have none. Whether those pages print a citation is for the image review to confirm.
ki_va_sus is Hebrew-only. Its idno is exodus/15/19 with the edition suffix, and its div has no corresp, so the only correspondence is the verse milestone. It has no English counterpart, as stated.

morning_song_shema marks the existing prayer child URN .../morning_song_shema/1 with unit=verse and n=4. The quotation is attributed to Deuteronomy 6:4 through seg@source. The surrounding prose sits outside the verse scope.

Not certified, left to the image/pointing review: the spelling of the divine name, which differs between files (יְיָ, ייָ, יְהֹוָה, and יהֹוָ with no sheva after the prefix בַּֽ/לַֽ); cantillation accents; the paseq in az_yashir 15:18; the period inside ki_va_sus 15:19 after הַיָּ֑ם; the period after וּבְתוֹרָתְךָ; אַתָּ and the missing maqaf in אַתָּה הוּא (Nehemiah 9:6); and the trailing period on the Hebrew citations.
Minor: the English ki_ladonai title says 'sovereignty' while its text says 'dominion'. This affects metadata only.
